chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Her first solo record for Jack Kapp
summary: She went to Chicago where Kapp recorded her playing what she thought was an audition. 'Night Life' became her first record, for which she was never paid.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I went back to Kansas City with the band and then Andy Kirk received a wire for them to come to Chicago. They went without me. They left me in Kansas City and what I did was join them because Jack Capp wouldn't record them without me.
Had you made any records by yourself at that time?

No. I think Jack Capp heard about me so I went there for him to hear me and while I was playing, thinking it was an audition, he recorded me, and that was 'Night Life'. I never got paid for it or anything. They put it out, 'Night Life' and the other thing, that was my first record.
And that was made at the same time as the Kirk records for Brunswick?
Now this I gather was all before you got to the Savoy and became a regular part of the -
No, we had been to the Savoy.
And you still weren't a regular part of the band?
No, the first time we went to the Savoy I wasn't a regular part of the band.
You told me about the time they called you to come in and take over -
We hadn't gone to the Pearl Theatre or recorded for Brunswick then.
I see, this all comes later.
